notes:
[TXT030-orders] Manuscript page 29 gives three monotonicity statements for F.G, separately for ≪, ≼ and ≤. The starred set description says F′.G={A∈F.G | A⊂|F′|}. The abbreviated explanation calls the operation Inf. Conditional on that greatest-lower-bound interpretation, the ordinary monotonicity argument for a) is valid; this is not a new existence proof. The readers’ individual targeted checks are recorded separately.

[TXT030-closure] The text attempts c) with “Prouvons c. Il faut prouver que” and “Prouvons que c’est fermé”. Its last step is valid if the cited theory of F.G really gives componentwise containment and if F′ is lower closed in F. Those premises are not established just by reading this page. In particular, inclusion of intersections does not in general imply either component inclusion for arbitrary sets; R2 checked the precise failure independently. The page’s figure-specific assertion is therefore retained as written, not replaced by a general-set claim. The repeated que, the literal “est le =” and the clipped L/G are preserved without grammatical or mathematical repair. A contextual enlargement removes the false prime in the cancelled A,A′∈F: that stroke descends from que above.

[TXT030-C7] The corollary says C6 is valable. The main line then says “Vérifions quand même C7₀”, with a visible small zero. The proposed extension is F′=G′∪(F\G), called réunion disjointe. Its three remaining tasks are explicitly listed after “Il faut vérifier”. The right note says “Un peu vif” and “mais il faut vérifier encore l’unicité”, then extracts two implications under “Cela amène à dégager”. No full verification of existence, figure structure, subdivision, or uniqueness is claimed by this run. The left note identifies the restriction with an inverse image.

[TXT030-ink] The lower-right boundary strokes are reproduced with TikZ around the complete marginal text and its tikz-cd square. The small inscription below-left of inverse phi, absent from both witnesses, remains Cor./où/omega; its position is preserved without interpreting it as a subscript. The starred word remains explication/explicitation/expliciter/explicitons, and the cancelled short word remains bien/i.e. The spelling def./déf. is uncertain at the accent. No date, title sheet or total-page statement occurs; manuscript number 29 is present.
